result.rationale: The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: group.js findMembers fires an async Discourse.ajax and in the .then handler unconditionally calls self.setProperties({user_count, limit, offset, members}) from the server response. Nothing in the controller's next/previous actions (admin-group.js) or the model cancels a prior in-flight request when a new one starts (e.g., no request-id guard or promise chaining on the model). Rapid pagination clicks can therefore have two requests in flight; the stale (earlier-offset) response can resolve last and overwrite members/offset/user_count with an older page.

adjudication.rationale: The findMembers function in group.js makes an async AJAX call and then sets properties on self (the model) when the promise resolves. If a user rapidly clicks next/previous pagination buttons, multiple requests can be in flight simultaneously. Since there's no request cancellation or sequencing mechanism, responses can arrive out of order. A slower request for page 1 could resolve after a faster request for page 2, causing the UI to display stale page 1 data while showing page 2's offset/pagination state. The diff shows this pattern clearly in the findMembers method at lines 27-42 where setProperties is called in the .then() callback without any guards against race conditions.
